subject: cap rate without guesswork
preheader: the formula is simple; the inputs still need evidence.
headline: Cap rate is modeled NOI divided by price. Verify both inputs.
body: Cap rate = Net Operating Income / Purchase Price. A $250,000 property with $20,000 in NOI is an 8% cap. That's the whole math.
A cap-rate comparison is only as useful as its NOI inputs and conventions. Check effective rent after vacancy and every applicable operating-expense line; do not silently treat unknown costs as zero.
There is no universal 'good' cap rate. Market, property condition, strategy, risk, and the evidence date all matter, so current local comparisons need a cited source and an as-of date.
Reconcile a seller's pro forma line by line with your own evidence. A difference can reveal different assumptions or definitions; by itself, it does not prove misrepresentation.
The practical cap-rate guide walks through effective income, vacancy, expense, and reserve assumptions before you run a preliminary property screen in TrueCap.
